q: Hashing in data structures (e.g., bloom filters) uses information-theoretic arguments. A Bloom filter with n elements, m bits, and k hash functions has false positive rate approximately:
exp: Bloom filter false positive rate: (1 − e^{-kn/m})^k ≈ (1/2)^k when k = (m/n) ln 2 (optimal k). This minimises false positives for given m and n. The optimal rate ≈ (0.6185)^{m/n}, which can be achieved with O((m/n) ln 2) hash functions.
